sections.content: SQL (Structured Query Language) talks to relational databases — tables of rows and columns. You use it to create tables, insert data, query it, update it, and delete it.
Relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite) store structured data with enforced types and relationships between tables.
Key points: SQL is declarative — you describe WHAT you want, not HOW to get it; most syntax is standard across engines with small dialect differences.
